evidence: server/services/client-review.service.ts:34-44 — ClientReviewError's code union is exactly INVALID_TOKEN | EXPIRED | REVOKED | ALREADY_RESOLVED | NOT_IDENTIFIED | NOT_INVITED | EMAIL_MISMATCH. requireLiveReview (:118-126) throws only three of them: INVALID_TOKEN when the row is missing, REVOKED when revokedAt is set, EXPIRED when expiresAt has passed; getReviewByToken (:132) is a straight call into it, so clientReview.get can produce nothing else. claim: The four dead-link boards draw the standard agency header, '{Agency} is asking for your feedback', like the rest of the family.
truth: On a dead link the product cannot know the agency, and does not try. The dead-link branch runs because the token query FAILED, so no payload — and therefore no agencyName — exists; the code passes the literal string 'Buildrick' into Shell, and the header renders 'Buildrick is asking for your feedback'. That is the one screen in the family where our name leads instead of the agency's, which inverts the rule the header exists to enforce (the code's own comment: 'The agency's name leads, not ours. The client hired them, not us.'), and it is the screen most likely to be seen by a stranger holding a broken link. All four boards draw '{Agency}' instead, so the boards specify a substitution the page cannot perform. D-H-04 and D-H-31 recorded this against the canonical family on page 1:6; against these four echoes it is unfiled.
